text:
​ @Kurozakki I don't really choose a dub unless it does something to enhance the experience or at least be on par with the Japanese dub. The average dub is serviceable at best, but most of the time the direction is bad so the lines come off as stilted and unnatural compared to their Japanese counterparts. I guess it helps that I'm learning Japanese, so I suppose to the average watcher, it won't be too offensively bad, but I typically choose sub because it just outperforms most dubs. Also if it's not set in Japan most of the time I will watch the dub, such as Monster. But even then some of the voices weren't great. 
My point is, most of the time the line deliveries sound inorganic enough to take me out of the experience. Not that there aren't bad Japanese dubs, because boy howdy there are, but they're just better across the board, with a couple exceptions.
